variables.name: STUDYID
variables.label: Study Identifier
variables.description: Unique identifier for a study.

variables.name: DOMAIN
variables.label: Domain Abbreviation
variables.description: Two-character abbreviation for the domain.

variables.name: USUBJID
variables.label: Unique Subject Identifier
variables.description: Identifier used to uniquely identify a subject across all studies for all applications or submissions involving the product.

variables.name: CESEQ
variables.label: Sequence Number
variables.description: Sequence number given to ensure uniqueness of subject records within a domain. May be any valid number.

variables.name: CEGRPID
variables.label: Group ID
variables.description: Used to link together a block of related records for a subject within a domain.

variables.name: CEREFID
variables.label: Reference ID
variables.description: Internal or external identifier (e.g., lab specimen ID, UUID for an ECG waveform or medical image).

variables.name: CESPID
variables.label: Sponsor-Defined Identifier
variables.description: Sponsor-defined identifier.

variables.name: CETERM
variables.label: Reported Term for the Clinical Event
variables.description: Term for the medical condition or event. Most likely preprinted on CRF.

variables.name: CEDECOD
variables.label: Dictionary-Derived Term
variables.description: Controlled terminology for the name of the clinical event. The sponsor is expected to provide the dictionary name and version used to map the terms utilizing the external codelist element in the Define-XML document.

variables.name: CECAT
variables.label: Category for the Clinical Event
variables.description: Used to define a category of related records.

variables.name: CESCAT
variables.label: Subcategory for the Clinical Event
variables.description: A further categorization of the condition or event.

variables.name: CEPRESP
variables.label: Clinical Event Pre-specified
variables.codelist: Version-agnostic anchor resource for codelist C66742
variables.description: Used to indicate whether the event in CETERM was prespecified. Value is "Y" for prespecified events and null for spontaneously reported events.

variables.name: CEOCCUR
variables.label: Clinical Event Occurrence
variables.codelist: Version-agnostic anchor resource for codelist C66742
variables.description: Used when the occurrence of specific events is solicited, to indicate whether or not a clinical event occurred. Values are null for spontaneously reported events.

variables.name: CESTAT
variables.label: Completion Status
variables.codelist: Version-agnostic anchor resource for codelist C66789
variables.description: The status indicates that a question from a prespecified list was not answered.

variables.name: CEREASND
variables.label: Reason Clinical Event Not Collected
variables.description: Describes the reason clinical event data was not collected. Used in conjunction with CESTAT when value is "NOT DONE".

variables.name: CEBODSYS
variables.label: Body System or Organ Class
variables.description: Dictionary-derived. Body system or organ class that is involved in an event or measurement from a standard hierarchy (e.g., MedDRA). When using a multi-axial dictionary such as MedDRA, this should contain the SOC used for the sponsor's analyses and summary tables, which may not necessarily be the primary SOC.

variables.name: CESEV
variables.label: Severity/Intensity
variables.codelist: Version-agnostic anchor resource for codelist C165643
variables.description: The severity or intensity of the event. Examples: "MILD", "MODERATE", "SEVERE".

variables.name: CETOXGR
variables.label: Standard Toxicity Grade
variables.description: Toxicity grade according to a standard toxicity scale (e.g., Common Terminology Criteria for Adverse Events (CTCAE) v3.0). Sponsor should specify name of the scale and version used in the metadata. If value is from a numeric scale, represent only the number (e.g., "2", not "Grade 2").

variables.name: TAETORD
variables.label: Planned Order of Element within Arm
variables.description: Number that gives the planned order of the element within the arm for the element in which the clinical event started.

variables.name: EPOCH
variables.label: Epoch
variables.codelist: Version-agnostic anchor resource for codelist C99079
variables.description: Epoch associated with the start date/time of the clinical event.

variables.name: CEDTC
variables.label: Date/Time of Event Collection
variables.description: Collection date and time for the clinical event observation represented in ISO 8601 character format.

variables.name: CESTDTC
variables.label: Start Date/Time of Clinical Event
variables.description: Start date/time of the clinical event represented in ISO 8601 character format.

variables.name: CEENDTC
variables.label: End Date/Time of Clinical Event
variables.description: End date/time of the clinical event, represented in ISO 8601 character format.

variables.name: CEDY
variables.label: Study Day of Event Collection
variables.description: Study day of clinical event collection, measured as integer days. Algorithm for calculations must be relative to the sponsor-defined RFSTDTC variable in Demographics. This formula should be consistent across the submission.

variables.name: CESTDY
variables.label: Study Day of Start of Event
variables.description: Actual study day of start of the clinical event expressed in integer days relative to the sponsor-defined RFSTDTC in Demographics.

variables.name: CEENDY
variables.label: Study Day of End of Event
variables.description: Actual study day of end of the clinical event expressed in integer days relative to the sponsor-defined RFSTDTC in Demographics.

variables.name: CESTRF
variables.label: Start Relative to Reference Period
variables.codelist: Version-agnostic anchor resource for codelist C66728
variables.description: Describes the start of the clinical event relative to the sponsor-defined reference period. The sponsor-defined reference period is a continuous period of time defined by a discrete starting point and a discrete ending point (represented by RFSTDTC and RFENDTC in Demographics). \n Not all values of the codelist are allowable for this variable. See Section 4.4.7, Use of Relative Timing Variables.

variables.name: CEENRF
variables.label: End Relative to Reference Period
variables.codelist: Version-agnostic anchor resource for codelist C66728
variables.description: Describes the end of the event relative to the sponsor-defined reference period. The sponsor-defined reference period is a continuous period of time defined by a discrete starting point and a discrete ending point (represented by RFSTDTC and RFENDTC in Demographics). \n Not all values of the codelist are allowable for this variable. See Section 4.4.7, Use of Relative Timing Variables.

variables.name: CESTRTPT
variables.label: Start Relative to Reference Time Point
variables.codelist: Version-agnostic anchor resource for codelist C66728
variables.description: Identifies the start of the observation as being before or after the reference time point defined by variable CESTTPT. \n Not all values of the codelist are allowable for this variable. See Section 4.4.7, Use of Relative Timing Variables.

variables.name: CESTTPT
variables.label: Start Reference Time Point
variables.description: Description or date/time in ISO 8601 character format of the sponsor-defined reference point referred to by --STRTPT. Examples: "2003-12-15", "VISIT 1".

variables.name: CEENRTPT
variables.label: End Relative to Reference Time Point
variables.codelist: Version-agnostic anchor resource for codelist C66728
variables.description: Identifies the end of the observation as being before or after the sponsor-defined reference time point defined by variable CEENTPT. \n Not all values of the codelist are allowable for this variable. See Section 4.4.7, Use of Relative Timing Variables.

variables.name: CEENTPT
variables.label: End Reference Time Point
variables.description: Description or date/time in ISO 8601 character format of the reference point referred to by CEENRTPT. Examples: "2003-12-25", "VISIT 2".
